gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Noto Sans Lisu has tiny gaps beneath its ascender tops. Its wide-open s curves keep a long passage moving smoothly, while Oxanium's ribbon-cut strokes stay the same width above.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian keeps its capitals barely taller than lowercase, with openings as wide as a sprung paper clip. And Oxanium's fixed-width brush line is what gives the pair its character, plain and unmistakable.

gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: The middle zone dominates each line here, with generous bends in the s. Oxanium does pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin, whereas Noto Sans Malayalam is best at settling into steady, approachable text.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Oxanium holds a tube-like thickness through every bend, and its high lowercase looks big. Noto Sans Mandaic, a plain sans, simply lets its curvy, unclamped letters do the reading.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Sharp, proud, almost capital-sized lowercase throughout. Noto Sans Marchen answers Oxanium's one-thickness traced glyphs with the same clear daylight at the end of its curves, and that shared openness is the pair's best trait.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-mayan-numera: Laser-etched lines, big lowercase, zero fuss. Noto Sans Mayan Numerals brings tall-bodied small letters and a visibly gaping c, so the heading's constant trace and the text's open shapes share the page easily.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-medefaidrin: Oxanium's pen line holds one width from start to finish, with a high x-height that makes its lowercase look big. And Noto Sans Medefaidrin, a plain sans, rises high too, with no ink pooling where its curves turn in.
